notes: Radius is to the cable (inner) surface or axis per each source; treat as minimums and use the governing (largest) applicable rule.
od_status 'verified' = value taken from a manufacturer catalogue or utility schedule, not a model; it has not been re-checked against a product drawing in this pass.
Source keys S1..S8 are listed in docs/cables-sources.md.

rules.source: Manufacturer UK installation note (2022) table for BS 7870-4.10 / 4.11 single-core 11-33 kV: dynamic 20 x OD (S2)
Same note: static 15 x OD, value taken from BS 6622:1999; controlled bend with a former, at joints and terminations (S2)
Same note, BS 6622 / BS 7835 single-core armoured 6.6-33 kV: dynamic 15 x OD (S2)

UK DNO policy NSP/002 v5.0 (Oct 2021) Table 8 gives XLPE 1c 33 kV 300/400/630 mm2 as 995/1070/1220 mm 'during and after installation'; about 19.3-19.7 x the catalogue OD, so ~20 x OD is derived here (S3)
AEIC/ICEA training radius for an assembly of three single 5-35 kV wire-shielded cables: F=5 x (2.155 x single-cable OD). US practice, final position only (S5)
UK DNO policy NSP/002 v5.0 Table 8, XLPE 1c 66 & 132 kV with solid metallic sheath, pulled into ducts: 35D (S3)
Same table, adjacent joints and terminations: 20D (S3)
Manufacturer UK installation note (2022): HV department advises of the order of 30 x D minimum for 66 kV and above (S2)
Public utility tender specification (2019), 132 kV 1c 630/1000 mm2: 20 x OD during installation (S7)
HV XLPE land cable user's guide rev 5, Table 19, laminated or lead sheathed design: at laying 18 De (S4)
Same Table 19, standard design (Cu wire screen only): at laying 15 De (S4)
No open source found for a 132 kV trefoil-specific rule; UK DNO table applies D per single cable regardless of formation (S3, S8)
